cache.name: cache
cache.basis: `evict n spacing` over a spacing sweep. N_evict(spacing) is fitted against an exact enumeration of which walk addresses land in the target's set, which yields the ways and the conflict period (sets x line) with no special case for sub-line, line-sized or aliasing spacings. The line used is the measured fetch granularity; where the period is larger, the split between sets and line is reported as undetermined rather than assumed
evidence: waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0: N_evict 4:8 8:4 16:2 32:1 64:1 128:1 256:1 512:1 1024:1 2048:1 4096:1 8192:1  -> 1-way, conflict period 32 B, 32 B (9/9 exact)

indexed: N_evict collapses to 1 at spacings that are multiples of 65536 B and is larger in between. No cache line is 65536 B, so that is an index period and the index is address bits [15:5]
tags vs bytes: with a 32 B fetch and a 65536 B conflict period the two models predict the same number (1), so the test cannot discriminate and no claim is made

replacement_policy.name: replacement_policy
replacement_policy.basis: the fitted geometry in every configuration measured
evidence: every configuration fits 1-way: waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0 1-way/period 32 B, waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=1 1-way/period 32 B, waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=2 1-way/period 32 B, waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=3 1-way/period 32 B
caveats: A direct-mapped cache has no replacement policy: the victim is the line the index selects, and no policy can choose otherwise. This is a measurement, not a gap.

knob_map.name: knob_map

latch.why: 8 of 8 matched pairs moved, 32Bx1 -> all-hit -- the probe reads uniformly fast, which hides the latch rather than removing it

data_reuse.why: 8 of 8 matched pairs moved, 1-way/period 32 B/32 B -> 1-way/period 65536 B/65536 B

knob_map.basis: the full cross-product: for each knob, every pair of measured configurations that differ in that knob alone is compared on three metrics (walk saturation, the fitted latch model, and the fitted cache geometry (ways, conflict period, capacity)). A knob 'controls' a structure when a matched pair moves it, 're-indexes' it when the geometry moves at constant capacity, and 'masks' it when the probe stops being able to see it
evidence: icache    -> read_width : no effect    identical in all 8 matched pairs
icache    -> latch      : no effect    identical in all 8 matched pairs
icache    -> data_reuse : no effect    identical in all 8 matched pairs
dcache    -> read_width : no effect    identical in all 8 matched pairs
dcache    -> latch      : masks        8 of 8 matched pairs moved, 32Bx1 -> all-hit -- the probe reads uniformly fast, which hides the latch rather than removing it
dcache    -> data_reuse : controls     8 of 8 matched pairs moved, 1-way/period 32 B/32 B -> 1-way/period 65536 B/65536 B
wrhighfreq -> read_width : no effect    identical in all 12 matched pairs
wrhighfreq -> latch      : no effect    identical in all 12 matched pairs
wrhighfreq -> data_reuse : no effect    identical in all 12 matched pairs
-> read width is moved by no knob, which is what makes it a property of the flash array rather than of the accelerator
-> no knob reaches the latch; dcache only masks it
-> multi-line data reuse is controlled by dcache and by nothing else

-> `icache` moved none of the three metrics. Every primitive here is a data access, so an instruction cache that does not share a structure with the data path is invisible to this probe by construction -- this is the expected reading for a separate I-cache, and it is not evidence that the register is inert. The instruction side is not measured: see the cache claim's caveats.

waitstate_scaling.name: waitstate_scaling
waitstate_scaling.basis: linear fit of the per-access cost against the `waitstates` knob, in each configuration separately; the headline coefficient is the latch differential in configuration 'dcache=0 icache=0 wrhighfreq=0'
evidence: dcache=0 icache=0 wrhighfreq=0: latch differential = 1.000 x WS + 0.000, R2=1.0000, worst residual 0.00 cyc (n=12)
dcache=0 icache=0 wrhighfreq=0: cold per-word cost = 1.000 x WS + 4.000, R2=1.0000 (n=12)
dcache=1 icache=1 wrhighfreq=3: latch differential = 0.000 x WS + 0.000, R2=1.0000, worst residual 0.00 cyc (n=12)
dcache=1 icache=1 wrhighfreq=3: cold per-word cost = 1.000 x WS + 4.000, R2=1.0000 (n=12)
caveats: A wait-state setting of 0 contributes a legitimate zero to this fit and must not be read as an absent structure: at LATENCY = 0 a hit and a miss cost the same cycle, so the structure is still there and simply worth nothing (MEASURING_CHANNELS B3).
At least one configuration shows a flat-zero differential at every wait state. That is the masking configuration (a cache holding both probe addresses), not evidence against the scaling.

twin_calibration.name: twin_calibration
twin_calibration.basis: the cold walk's `flash - twin` per-access cost measured at `waitstates = 0`, where a flash access is known to cost no more than an SRAM one, so anything left over is the harness. Computed per configuration and per loop body and never pooled across either; the headline is the isolated configuration, which is the one the structural claims are measured in
evidence: waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0: `reread` body over 6 point(s) -> flash-twin = +3.000 cyc/access
waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0: `walk` body over 2 point(s) -> flash-twin = +4.000 cyc/access
waitstates=0 icache=1 dcache=1 wrhighfreq=3: `reread` body over 6 point(s) -> flash-twin = +1.000 cyc/access
waitstates=0 icache=1 dcache=1 wrhighfreq=3: `walk` body over 2 point(s) -> flash-twin = +4.000 cyc/access
caveats: The twin is NOT a zero here: at `waitstates = 0`, where a flash access cannot cost more than an SRAM one, `flash - twin` still reads +4.000 cycles per access in waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0. A NEGATIVE value means the flash buffer measures CHEAPER than its own SRAM twin, which is the bus-port signature: the probe loop runs from SRAM, so SRAM *data* loads contend with the loop's own instruction fetch while flash data loads sit on another port. Every figure derived by subtracting the twin in this configuration carries that bias, and correcting means subtracting it. The instrument-neutral quantity is `flash(LATENCY) - flash(0)` at the same stride, which cancels the loop entirely.

The single-`reread` body reads +2.000 cycles in the same configuration, against +4.000 for the `walk` body. One number per (configuration, loop body) is the smallest honest unit: a longer loop body has idle cycles for an extra bus beat to hide in, so the two bodies are not interchangeable and are not averaged into one figure.

notes: Cross-check: the latch granularity equals the flash read width (32 B), as it does on every part in this repository.

INSTRUMENT: in waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0 the SRAM twin is offset by +4.000 cycles per access at zero wait states, so every twin-subtracted figure measured in that configuration carries that bias -- correcting means subtracting it. The offset is NOT the same in every configuration and is not pooled; see the twin_calibration claim for the per-configuration table.
